subject: Peaks.ai — latency cascade affecting long-tail completions (customer impact)
messages:
From: Carlos Alvarez <c.alvarez@peaksai.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: PeaksOps Pager <pager@peaksops.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in long-tail completions — real customer impact

Marcus —

We started seeing a spike in completions >15s for a subset of inference requests starting late last night. The frontend shows increased queues and some calls are timing out at 30s. This is affecting our live recommendation sync: about 6% of completions are now >15s and a few customers reported slow page loads.

Attached is a short sample of the slow traces and the Kibana links in the body. Can you triage? Our SRE is also on the pager but asked to get your team involved because the patterns look like internal queuing.

Attachments: latency_sample_20260627.txt

— Carlos
Director of Engineering, Peaks.ai
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Alvarez <c.alvarez@peaksai.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, PeaksOps Pager <pager@peaksops.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in long-tail completions — real customer impact

Carlos — thanks for the heads up and the samples. We see the same on our telemetry (p95 fine, heavy p99 tail growth). Looping in Dev for a deep look.

Immediate asks:
- Monica, can you pull a svc-metrics snapshot (token service + queue lengths + host CPU/GPU) for 00:00–08:00 UTC and attach?
- Dev, please check recent routing changes and concurrency cap metrics for Peaks.ai routing policy. Any quick mitigations (shorter cache TTLs, soft-reject thresholds) we can apply safely?

I’ll set an internal sync at 10:00 PT and keep Carlos updated.

— Marcus
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: PeaksOps Pager <pager@peaksops.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in long-tail completions — real customer impact

Attached: svc-metrics-snapshot-0628.json

Quick summary from the snapshot:
- Queue length on Peaks.ai route spiked ~3x between 01:15–02:20 UTC.
- A small subset of requests were funneled to a cluster with an older kernel/quantization path (nodepool-legacy-3). That pool shows higher per-token latency and KV cache miss rate.
- Concurrency caps for the route were at 120; we hit sustained saturation for ~40 minutes.
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) remained low, but time-to-first-token increased significantly for the affected pool.

Next (immediate): recommend moving traffic away from nodepool-legacy-3 and temporarily lowering concurrency cap to 90 to reduce in-flight buildup while we diagnose why that pool had KV cache misses.

— Monica
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Carlos Alvarez <c.alvarez@peaksai.com>
Cc: PeaksOps Pager <pager@peaksops.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in long-tail completions — real customer impact

On Sun, 28 Jun 2026 at 09:50 AM monica_patel wrote:
> Attached: svc-metrics-snapshot-0628.json
> 
> Quick summary from the snapshot:
> - Queue length on Peaks.ai route spiked ~3x between 01:15–02:20 UTC.
> - A small subset of requests were funneled to a cluster with an older kernel/quantization path (nodepool-legacy-3) ...

Thanks — that aligns with what I’m seeing in the runtime logs. Root cause hypothesis: nodepool-legacy-3 recently picked up a model variant that has an extra KV cache warming step due to a model-layer reorder in the build. Under normal load it’s fine, but when traffic funnels there it causes extra blocking on KV acquisition which cascades to queueing and increases tail latency.

Immediate mitigations we applied at 10:05 PT:
- Reroute 100% of Peaks.ai traffic off nodepool-legacy-3 to nodepool-standard-7.
- Bumped soft concurrency cap for Peaks.ai to 140 briefly to allow the reroute to drain without hard rejects (monitoring closely).
- Purged stale per-shard KV entries for the legacy pool and disabled the variant rollout.

Monitoring notes: tails dropped within ~6 minutes after the reroute; p99 returned to baseline at ~10:14 PT. We’ll keep the reroute in place until we test a patched kernel and confirm KV warmup behavior is corrected.

Carlos — sorry for the impact. We’ll coordinate a postmortem and a scheduled maintenance window to roll the fix.

— Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Alvarez <c.alvarez@peaksai.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, PeaksOps Pager <pager@peaksops.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in long-tail completions — real customer impact

Carlos —

Follow-up and executive summary for your leadership:

What happened: A targeted funneling of traffic routed a portion of Peaks.ai traffic to nodepool-legacy-3 which runs an older kernel that triggers an extra KV warm step for a newly onboarded model variant. Under a transient surge this caused in-flight buildup and long-tail completion increases (p99).

What we did: Immediate reroute off the legacy pool, purged stale KV entries, and disabled the rollout. That produced p99 recovery within ~10 minutes. We will:
- Schedule a maintenance window to patch the kernel and re-validate the model variant (proposed 2026-07-02 22:00 UTC).
- Provide a short postmortem with timeline + corrective actions (by 2026-07-01 EOD).
- Offer Peaks.ai a one-month credit for impacted units; LMK if that is acceptable and I’ll route through finance.

Status now: service stable; we continue to monitor auto-scaling headroom and KV cache miss signals. Monica and Dev will run a deeper replay and share a mitigation checklist for routing policy hardening.

If your execs want an on-call briefing, I can join a 30m sync tomorrow.

— Marcus
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
